summary: Declares RFC 2731, on encoding Dublin Core metadata in HTML, obsolete, because further work on it moved to the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative. It is a short informational notice that retires the older document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2731 described how to put Dublin Core metadata in HTML. The work later moved to newer specifications from the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative, so RFC 5791 declares RFC 2731 obsolete.

questions: where did dublin core html encoding move
what is dublin core metadata in html
what is the successor to rfc 2731
subtitle: RFC 2731 is obsolete because Dublin Core metadata work moved to the DCMI.

tldr.problem: RFC 2731 described encoding Dublin Core metadata in HTML, but newer specifications from the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative had superseded that work.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5791 obsoletes RFC 2731 and points implementers to the DCMI's HTML/XHTML meta and link element specification.
tldr.outcome: The newer specification adds a requirement concerning the profile attribute of the head element.

today: RFC 5791 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 2731. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why RFC 2731 Is Obsolete
sections.content:
RFC 2731 defines encoding Dublin Core metadata in HTML. The Dublin Core Metadata Initiative published newer specifications over the following decade, including one on expressing Dublin Core metadata with HTML and XHTML meta and link elements.

RFC 5791 obsoletes RFC 2731 because further development of that specification moved to the DCMI.
sections.plainLanguage: Newer DCMI specifications superseded the HTML metadata approach in RFC 2731. This memo records that the IETF document is obsolete.

sections.title: The Successor Specification
sections.content:
The cited successor is titled "Expressing Dublin Core metadata using HTML/XHTML meta and link elements" and was published by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative in August 2008.

The memo notes that implementers of RFC 2731 should pay attention to the newer specification's requirement concerning the profile attribute of the head element.
sections.plainLanguage: The DCMI document is the newer reference for expressing this metadata in HTML or XHTML. It changes a requirement related to the head element's profile attribute.

sections.title: Administrative Status
sections.content: RFC 5791 describes itself as administrative in nature. Its security section says there are no security relations related to the memo.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo records an administrative change and says it has no related security considerations.

references.text: Kunze, J., "Encoding Dublin Core Metadata in HTML", RFC 2731, December 1999.
Johnston, P. and A. Powell, "Expressing Dublin Core metadata using HTML/XHTML meta and link elements", Dublin Core Metadata Initiative, August 2008.
